create_embeddings.description: Turn texts into vectors for semantic search, finding similar items or clustering, ready to store in a vector database.
create_embeddings.name: create_embeddings

parameters.description: The texts to embed, one per entry. Each comes back as one vector, in the same order.
parameters.name: texts

parameters.description: Which embedding model to use. Defaults to mistral-embed.
parameters.name: model

parameters.description: How many numbers each vector has, for a vector database that expects a set size. Only Codestral Embed can change it, up to 3,072. Leave blank for the model's own size.
parameters.name: dimensions

dimensions.description: How many numbers each vector has.

embeddings.description: One vector per text, in the same order.

extract_document_data.description: Pull the fields you name, such as an invoice's number, date and total, out of a PDF, Word or PowerPoint file, or a photo or scan. A field the document doesn't contain comes back empty rather than guessed.

extract_document_data.name: extract_document_data

parameters.description: The document to read: upload a file, pick one an earlier step produced, or paste a link to one. PDFs, Word and PowerPoint files, and images such as photos or scans all work, up to 50 MB and 1,000 pages.
parameters.name: document

parameters.description: The pieces of information you want back, one per entry. Add what each means after a colon to steer it: 'total: the amount due, with its currency'.

examples.label: An invoice
examples.value: ["invoice number", "invoice date", "vendor", "total: the amount due, with its currency"]

parameters.name: fields

parameters.description: Optional guidance on how to fill the fields, such as 'Write dates as YYYY-MM-DD' or 'Give amounts without a currency symbol'.
parameters.name: instructions

parameters.description: Which pages to read, counting from 1, such as '1-3, 5'. Leave blank to read every page.
parameters.name: pages

data.description: Each field you named, with its value from the document, or empty when the document doesn't contain it.

missing_fields.description: The fields the document doesn't contain.

model.description: The Mistral OCR model that read the document.

text.description: The text of every page read, as Markdown, from the same pass.

parameters.description: The document to read: upload a file, pick one an earlier step produced, or paste a link to one. PDFs, Word and PowerPoint files, and images such as photos or scans all work, up to 50 MB and 1,000 pages.
parameters.name: document

parameters.description: Which pages to read, counting from 1, such as '1-3, 5'. Leave blank to read every page.
parameters.name: pages

parameters.description: Drop the text repeated at the top and bottom of each page, such as running titles and page numbers, so it doesn't interrupt the body text.
parameters.display_name: Leave out page headers and footers
parameters.name: remove_headers_and_footers

model.description: The Mistral OCR model that read the document.

generate_model_response.description: Send a prompt to a Mistral AI model and get back its written response.

mock_response.response_text: Here is a thoughtful response to your question about artificial intelligence and its applications in modern software development.

generate_model_response.name: generate_model_response

parameters.description: The message or question to send to Mistral.
parameters.name: prompt

parameters.description: Optional instructions that set the model's role, tone, or output format for this request (e.g. 'You are a concise support agent. Reply in two sentences.').
parameters.name: system_prompt

parameters.description: Which Mistral model to use. Defaults to mistral-large-latest. Mistral's free plan leaves out Mistral Large, Medium and Small; Ministral and Codestral work on it.
parameters.name: model

parameters.description: Maximum number of tokens Mistral may generate in its response. Raise it for longer replies. Leave blank to use the model's own default.
parameters.name: max_tokens

parameters.description: How varied the response should be, from 0 (focused and predictable) to 1.5 (more creative). Mistral recommends staying between 0 and 0.7. Leave blank to use the model's own default.
parameters.name: temperature

completion_tokens.description: Number of tokens the response used.

finish_reason.description: Why the model stopped generating, e.g. 'stop' when it finished or 'length' when it hit the response limit.

model.description: The Mistral model that produced the response.

prompt_tokens.description: Number of tokens the prompt used.

response_text.description: The text Mistral generated for your prompt.

total_tokens.description: Total tokens billed for this request.

list_models.description: List the Mistral models your API key can use, including your fine-tuned ones, with what each can do, how much text it takes in, and when Mistral plans to retire it.
list_models.name: list_models

parameters.description: Only list models that can do this, such as read images or transcribe audio. Leave on 'Anything' for every model.
parameters.name: capability

model_ids.description: Every model's id, in the same order.

aliases.description: Other ids for the same model, such as its '-latest' alias.

capabilities.description: What it can do, like 'chat', 'vision' or 'ocr'.

deprecation_date.description: When Mistral plans to retire it, or empty.

id.description: The id to use the model by.

max_context_length.description: How many tokens it can take in at once.

replacement_model.description: The model Mistral suggests moving to, or empty.

type.description: 'base' for Mistral's own models, 'fine-tuned' for yours.

moderate_text.description: Check text against Mistral's moderation categories, such as hate, violence, self-harm, personal data and jailbreak attempts, and get back which it falls into, with a score for each.
moderate_text.name: moderate_text

parameters.description: The text to check, such as a customer message, a review or an AI-written reply.
parameters.name: text

parameters.description: Optional: the message the text answers, such as the question an AI-written reply responds to. Mistral then judges the text in that context, so a reply can be flagged for what it helps with, not just what it says.
parameters.name: in_reply_to

categories.description: Every category, true when the text falls into it.

flagged.description: Whether the text falls into any category.

flagged_categories.description: The categories the text falls into, like 'pii' or 'violence_and_threats'.

highest_category.description: The category with the highest score.

model.description: The moderation model that checked the text.

transcribe_audio.description: Turn a recording, such as a call, meeting or voice note, into text with Mistral's Voxtral, optionally labelled by speaker and timestamped.

segments.speaker: speaker_1
segments.text: Thanks for calling Acme support, this is Dana.

segments.speaker: speaker_2
segments.text: Hi Dana, my invoice shows the wrong total.

mock_response.text: Thanks for calling Acme support, this is Dana. Hi Dana, my invoice shows the wrong total.
mock_response.transcript_by_speaker:
speaker_1: Thanks for calling Acme support, this is Dana.
speaker_2: Hi Dana, my invoice shows the wrong total.

transcribe_audio.name: transcribe_audio

parameters.description: The recording to transcribe: upload a file, pick one an earlier step produced, or paste a link to one. Recordings of up to about three hours work.
parameters.name: audio

parameters.description: The language being spoken. Leave it on automatic detection unless the recording is short or noisy enough to fool it.
parameters.name: language

parameters.description: Label who said what, so the transcript reads as a conversation. Mistral then times the transcript by segment.
parameters.name: identify_speakers

parameters.description: Note when each part was said, by segment (a phrase or sentence) or by word. With speakers identified, only segments can be timed.
parameters.name: timestamps

parameters.description: Names, jargon or product terms the recording uses, so they're spelled right: one per entry, up to 100 words. A phrase is listened for word by word.
parameters.name: words_to_listen_for

duration_seconds.description: How long the recording is, in seconds.

language.description: The language spoken, as a code like 'en', when Mistral reports it or you set it.

model.description: The Voxtral model that transcribed it.

segments.description: The transcript in timed stretches (segments, or single words with word timestamps), each with who said it when speakers were identified. Filled when you ask for speakers or timestamps.

speaker.description: Who said it, like 'speaker_1', when speakers were identified.

speakers.description: Each speaker, in the order they first spoke.

transcript_by_speaker.description: The transcript with one line per turn, like 'speaker_1: …', when speakers were identified.

description: Use Mistral AI in your workflows: answer questions and write text with its chat models, read documents and pull data out of them with Mistral OCR, transcribe recordings with Voxtral, moderate content, and create embeddings for semantic search.
